title: The Appointment That Began Before the Visit
title_ja: 診察前から始まった受診
fact_notes: 人物・施設・活動・結果は架空の事例。実在の統計や研究結果ではない。医療・宇宙工学の実用的な手順や効果を示すものではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり、実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A fictional neighborhood clinic invited several patients to discuss how they prepared for ordinary medical appointments.
sentences.ja: 架空の地域診療所は、通常の診察に向けてどのように準備するか患者数人に話してもらった。

sentences.en: One patient explained that she often remembered an important question only after leaving the doctor's office.
sentences.ja: ある患者は診察室を出てから重要な質問を思い出すことがよくあると説明した。

sentences.en: Another said that he brought a long list of concerns but found it difficult to explain which mattered most to him.
sentences.ja: 別の患者は心配事の長い一覧を持参したが、どれが最も重要か説明するのが難しいと語った。

sentences.en: The clinic staff wondered whether a small change before the visit could make the conversation easier for both patients and professionals.
sentences.ja: 診療所の職員は受診前の小さな変更が患者と医療従事者の双方の会話をしやすくするか考えた。

sentences.en: Instead of developing a complicated application, the staff prepared an optional sheet that patients could use at home.
sentences.ja: 複雑なアプリを開発する代わりに、患者が自宅で使える任意の用紙を用意した。

sentences.en: The sheet invited patients to describe their main concern in their own words and write down questions they hoped to discuss.
sentences.ja: 用紙には主な心配事を自分の言葉で説明し、相談したい質問を書き留めるよう案内があった。

sentences.en: It also provided a space for information that patients wished to bring to the attention of the medical team.
sentences.ja: 医療チームに伝えたい情報を書く欄もあった。

sentences.en: The staff made clear that filling in the sheet was not a condition for receiving medical care.
sentences.ja: 用紙の記入が医療を受ける条件ではないことを明確にした。

sentences.en: During a short trial, some patients completed the sheet while others preferred to prepare notes in their own way.
sentences.ja: 短期間の試行で用紙を記入する患者もいれば、自分の方法でメモを準備する患者もいた。

sentences.en: A receptionist offered assistance to people who had difficulty reading or writing the form, whenever they requested it.
sentences.ja: 受付職員は読み書きが難しい人から依頼があれば記入を手伝った。

sentences.en: The clinic also allowed patients to discuss their notes privately with a professional rather than hand them in at the reception desk.
sentences.ja: 診療所は受付で提出せず、医療従事者と個別にメモを話し合うことも認めた。

sentences.en: This option was important because the notes might contain personal information that patients did not wish to share publicly.
sentences.ja: メモには患者が公に共有したくない個人情報が含まれる可能性があるため、この選択肢は重要だった。

sentences.en: After the trial, the staff collected feedback about whether the sheet had helped patients communicate what they wanted to say.
sentences.ja: 試行後、職員は用紙が患者の伝えたいことの伝達に役立ったか意見を集めた。

sentences.en: Several people found the prompts useful, but others suggested reducing the number of questions printed on the page.
sentences.ja: 質問の手がかりが役立った人もいたが、印刷する質問数を減らすよう提案する人もいた。

sentences.en: The staff revised the sheet and continued to offer it as one possible tool rather than as a requirement.
sentences.ja: 職員は用紙を修正し、必須ではなく選択可能な道具として提供し続けた。

sentences.en: They did not measure medical outcomes and therefore made no claim that using the form improved anyone's health.
sentences.ja: 健康上の結果は測定していないので、用紙の利用が誰かの健康を改善したとは主張しなかった。

sentences.en: The project reminded the clinic that good communication begins before a conversation as well as during it.
sentences.ja: 活動は良いコミュニケーションが会話の最中だけでなくその前から始まることを診療所に思い出させた。

sentences.en: Preparation may help some individuals express concerns, but a prepared form cannot replace attentive listening.
sentences.ja: 準備は心配事を伝える助けになる場合もあるが、用紙が注意深く聴くことの代わりにはならない。

sentences.en: A useful support tool should make participation easier without creating a new barrier for people who cannot use it.
sentences.ja: 有用な支援道具は、それを使えない人に新たな障壁を作らず参加を容易にすべきだ。

sentences.en: For the staff, the central goal remained understanding each patient's needs rather than collecting completed sheets.
sentences.ja: 職員にとって主な目的は記入済み用紙の回収ではなく、各患者の必要性を理解することだった。

questions.prompt: What problem did one patient describe?
options: Being unable to find the clinic's building.
Receiving a long list of medicines at every visit.
Remembering a question only after leaving the doctor's office.
Being required to write a report before going home.
questions.explanation_ja: 診察後に質問を思い出した。

questions.prompt: What difficulty did another patient mention?
options: Explaining which concern mattered most to him.
Getting permission to enter the clinic.
Finding a place to buy a notebook.
Remembering the name of every staff member.
questions.explanation_ja: 重要な心配事を説明しづらかった。

options: A compulsory application for every patient.
A medical examination for family members.
A public list of all patients' concerns.
An optional sheet for use before a visit.
questions.explanation_ja: 任意の準備用紙を作った。

questions.prompt: Why did staff clarify that the sheet was not a condition for care?
options: To prevent patients from preparing questions.
To avoid making the form an obstacle to receiving help.
To encourage only wealthy patients to visit.
To require everyone to complete it at reception.
questions.explanation_ja: 用紙が受診の障壁にならないようにした。

questions.prompt: What help could a receptionist provide on request?
options: Assistance with reading or writing the form.
An independent diagnosis of the patient's condition.
A guarantee of improved health.
A prescription without a medical visit.

questions.prompt: Why could patients discuss notes privately?
options: All reception staff had been dismissed.
The clinic had forbidden patients to write anything.
The notes might contain information they did not want others to know.
The notes always contained irrelevant information.

questions.prompt: What improvement did some users suggest?
options: Making the form compulsory.
Reducing the number of printed questions.
Adding every patient's name to a public list.
Removing the option to ask questions.

questions.prompt: Why did staff make no claim about health improvement?
options: They knew every user's health had become worse.
They had measured all possible outcomes.
They had stopped offering the sheet completely.
They had not measured medical outcomes.
questions.explanation_ja: 健康上の結果を測っていない。

options: Carefully paying attention.
Immediately ending a conversation.
Speaking as loudly as possible.
Following a printed form without thinking.
questions.explanation_ja: 注意をよく払うという意味。

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects the passage?
options: Every patient must prepare a written form before receiving care.
Written notes can replace conversations with medical professionals.
Preparation tools should support communication without excluding people who cannot use them.
Completing a form proves that a person's health has improved.
questions.explanation_ja: 準備道具で参加を支えつつ新たな障壁を作らない。

paraphrases.source: The clinic staff wondered whether a small change before the visit could make the conversation easier for both patients and professionals.
paraphrases.rewrite: The staff considered whether adjusting the preparation process might improve communication for both sides.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 受診前の工夫が双方の会話を助けるか検討。

paraphrases.source: The staff made clear that filling in the sheet was not a condition for receiving medical care.
paraphrases.rewrite: The clinic explained that people could receive care even if they did not fill out the sheet.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 未記入でも受診できる。

paraphrases.source: The clinic also allowed patients to discuss their notes privately with a professional rather than hand them in at the reception desk.
paraphrases.rewrite: Patients could choose to show their notes directly to a professional in private instead of submitting them at the front desk.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 受付提出の代わりに個別相談を選べた。

paraphrases.source: A useful support tool should make participation easier without creating a new barrier for people who cannot use it.
paraphrases.rewrite: Support should make participation more accessible rather than impose a new difficulty on people unable to use the tool.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 支援が新たな障壁にならないことが大切。
